national_news.title: India-EU Trade Pact and Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism Challenges
bullets: India and the European Union concluded negotiations for a major Free Trade Agreement (FTA) in January 2026.
The EU's Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) entered its definitive financial phase concurrently, posing potential policy friction.
Differences in carbon cost measurement and recognition between Indian domestic regulations and EU's CBAM risk imposing a double compliance burden on Indian exporters, threatening FTA gains.

national_news.title: Centre Approves Qadian-Beas Railway Line Project in Punjab
bullets: The Centre approved a detailed estimate of ₹1,419.05 crore for the 39.68 km Qadian-Beas broad gauge railway line in Punjab's Majha region.
The project will be executed by Northern Railway and includes infrastructure like two crossing stations (Ghuman and Butala), 11 major bridges, 121 minor bridges, and 54 Road Under Bridges (RUBs).
The corridor will also feature the deployment of Kavach, India's indigenous train collision avoidance system, and serves as an alternative strategic route for the Amritsar–Pathankot section.

national_news.title: India Leads Global Areca Nut Production
bullets: India is the world's largest producer of areca nut (betel nut), accounting for approximately 63% of total global production in 2025-26 according to the Directorate of Arecanut and Spices Development (DASD).
Total arecanut cultivation area reached 11.06 lakh hectares with a production of 15.29 lakh tonnes in 2025-26, up from 14.91 lakh tonnes in the previous year.
Karnataka is the largest producing state in India, yielding about 10 lakh tonnes, followed by Kerala, Assam, Meghalaya, Mizoram, West Bengal, and Tamil Nadu.

national_news.title: Overview and History of the News Services Division of All India Radio
bullets: The News Services Division (NSD) of AIR operates under the motto 'Bahujan Hitaya, Bahujan Sukhaya', delivering news 24/7 across major languages and dialects.
The first news bulletin in India was broadcast on July 23, 1927, from the Bombay Station under the Indian Broadcasting Company, which later became All India Radio on June 8, 1936.
NSD currently broadcasts 607 daily bulletins totaling 3,150 minutes across 92 languages and dialects, including foreign language transmissions like Arabic, French, and Chinese.

national_news.title: All India Radio Broadcasting Code and Election Coverage Guidelines
bullets: The All India Radio (AIR) Broadcasting Code prohibits criticism of friendly countries, attacks on religions, obscenity, defamation, incitement to violence, and contempt of court.
The code bars aspersions against the integrity of the President, Governors, and the Judiciary, as well as hostile criticism of any State or Central Government policies that amount to personal tirade.

The Election Commission recognizes the crucial role of electronic media and mandates strict guidelines, prohibiting the projection of only a single candidate per constituency and requiring balanced coverage of campaigns and party manifestos.

The syndicate was planning subversive terror attacks ahead of Independence Day through grenade, IED, and petrol bomb attacks as well as targeted espionage.
Substantial recoveries including IEDs, Pakistan Ordnance Factory-marked grenades, and firearms were made, with cases booked under the UAPA and Arms Act.

The agreement entails leasing two MQ-9B Sea Guardian High-Altitude Long-Endurance (HALE) Remotely Piloted Aircraft Systems for 30 months.
The acquisition significantly strengthens the Indian Navy's Maritime Domain Awareness, intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance capabilities across the Indian Ocean Region.

national_news.title: Customs Officials Seize Gold Worth Rs 2.65 Crore at Chennai Airport, Two Myanmar Nationals Arrested
bullets: Customs Air Intelligence Unit (AIU) at Anna International Airport in Chennai seized 1,967 grams of 24-karat gold valued at Rs 2.65 crore.

The accused were remanded to judicial custody under the provisions of the Customs Act, 1962.

national_news.title: DRI Uncovers Rs 2,500 Crore Customs Duty Fraud in Areca Nut Imports
bullets: The Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI) dismantled a major smuggling network involving areca nut imports from Southeast Asia falsely declared as Bangladeshi origin.
The operation uncovered a potential revenue loss of over Rs 2,500 crore by fraudulently availing concessional duty benefits under the South Asian Free Trade Area (SAFTA).
Nine persons have been arrested, Rs 75 lakh in cash and 160 metric tonnes of areca nuts were seized, and the license of the primary Customs Broker firm was suspended.

national_news.title: DRI Uncovers Major Areca Nut Import Scam Exploiting SAFTA Agreement
bullets: The Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI) under the Ministry of Finance uncovered a major smuggling syndicate defrauding the exchequer of over Rs 2,500 crore.

Syndicates illegally imported areca nuts from South-East Asian countries (Indonesia, Thailand, Malaysia) by mis-declaring their origin as Bangladesh to fraudulently claim duty exemptions under the South Asian Free Trade Area (SAFTA) agreement.
Areca nut imports normally attract a Basic Customs Duty (BCD) of 100%, whereas eligible imports under SAFTA from Bangladesh enjoy complete exemption.
Operations led to the arrest of nine persons, seizure of about Rs 75 lakh in cash and 160 metric tonnes of areca nuts, and suspension of the license of the involved Customs Broker firm.
